meta.title: Evidence Bank
meta.scope: What President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration has delivered for the South-East since May 2023.
summary: Its own federal development commission, the South East Development Commission (SEDC)
Thirteen top federal posts, including Foreign Affairs and Works
About ₦87bn paid or invested straight into its students, borrowers, small businesses and campuses
43 federal road projects under way (1,704 km) and 10 completed, backed by more than ₦1.5 trillion of road contracts revived, approved or started
128 emergency road repairs completed across the five states
The Port Harcourt–Aba railway running again
meta.methodology: Compiled by the South-East Political Appointees Forum (SEPAF) from government sources, agency reports, a South-East road projects status workbook (as at 18 October 2026) and established Nigerian media, as at 9 November 2026. Every item links to its sources. Items are ranked by impact: scale, people reached and visibility in the South-East. “Completed” means delivered; “Ongoing”, “Approved / funded” and “Announced” mark work that is not yet complete. Where a South-East figure is derived as a share of a national total, the share is shown.

metrics.label: South-Easterners in top federal posts, three at the very top

metrics.label: 2026 budget for the zone's own federal development commission
metrics.detail: SEDC Act signed July 2024 · board inaugurated Feb 2025 · ₦140bn federal + ₦25bn from the five governors · South East Investment Company with a ₦150bn+ capital target.

metrics.label: new federal universities and colleges
metrics.detail: Running: Alvan Ikoku Federal University of Education (Owerri), Federal University of Allied Health Sciences (Enugu). Signed into law: FUMHS Item and FCE Bende (Abia), Federal University Okigwe (Imo), Federal University of Agriculture Ako-Nike (Enugu).

metrics.label: homes and student beds approved or under way
metrics.detail: 1,700 Renewed Hope homes (Umuahia 1,200, Bende 250, Ezza North 250) · 5,468 student hostel beds at ESUT, UNN, FUTO and Fed Poly Nekede.

metrics.label: Port Harcourt–Aba railway rebuilt, with trains running since May 2024
metrics.detail: Part of the US$3.02bn Eastern line. Handed to the NRC in November 2024.

metrics.label: Aba power plant commissioned; 4 of 5 states now run their own power markets
metrics.detail: Aba Integrated Power Project (Feb 2024) · ANOH gas plant, Imo (May 2024) · Electricity Act 2023: Enugu first in Nigeria, then Imo, Abia and Anambra.

achievements.title: Federal roads in the South-East: 10 projects completed, 43 under way and 128 emergency repairs done
achievements.figure: Completed: 10 projects, 342.8 km (5 new, 5 inherited). Ongoing: 43 projects, 1,704.2 km (22 new, 21 inherited); 677.0 km of it done. Total completed length (full and partial) 1,019.8 km. Bridges: 10. Emergency repairs completed: 128
achievements.description: As at 18 October 2026, 10 federal road and bridge projects in the South-East had been completed (342.8 km, counting both carriageways on dual roads) and 43 were under way (1,704.2 km). Work on the ongoing projects had covered a further 677 km, bringing completed length, full and partial, to about 1,019.8 km. Ten bridges were completed or under way, and 128 emergency repair and special intervention projects (palliatives) had been finished across the five states. Of the 53 completed and ongoing projects, 27 are new contracts and 26 were inherited.
achievements.creditedTo: Federal Government; Federal Ministry of Works

achievements.title: Enugu–Onitsha Expressway: 214 km of dual carriageway; Enugu section completed and the road 74% done

achievements.description: The stalled Enugu–Onitsha dual carriageway was put back on a deadline (originally 10 May 2026) under MTN's road tax-credit scheme, and about 72 km was redesigned in reinforced concrete. Works Minister Umahi opened the first 15 km concrete section to traffic for Easter on 2 April 2026, while the 18 km and 39 km concrete sections were still under construction.
